results.body:
Found reviewing #661.

`sssom_grading.CONFIDENCE` emits only two values — `0.99` for `EXACT_MATCH`/`SYNONYM_MATCH`, `0.9` for every other quality. The published set carries four:

```
0.99: 2068    0.9: 858    0.8: 50    0.95: 45
```

The 95 off-table rows are uniform: all `skos:exactMatch`, all to CHEBI, all `semapv:LexicalMatching`.

```
MIM:2-mercaptoethanesulfonate -> CHEBI:17905  conf=0.95
MIM:Acetate                   -> CHEBI:30089  conf=0.95
MIM:Alcl3                     -> CHEBI:30114  conf=0.8
MIM:Alk_So42                  -> CHEBI:86463  conf=0.8
```

They look like a graded lexical-matching pass that predates the current table — a per-row score rather than a per-quality constant.

**Why it is worth recording:** no code path produces these values and none validates them. They are identity rows, so #661's new GRADE check deliberately skips them (MAPPING_SEMANTICS §Rule D: an own-identifier row must be `skos:exactMatch` regardless of `mapping_quality`), and `_sync_quality_columns` would overwrite them with `0.99` the moment anything did touch them. So the corpus holds 95 rows of unreachable state that would silently change meaning on the next reconcile that happened to include them.

Not a defect in #661 and not a blocker — the rows are internally consistent and Rule D is satisfied. The question is whether the values are deliberate provenance worth preserving (in which case `_sync_quality_columns` would erase them) or residue worth normalising.

**Suggested disposition:** decide one way or the other, then either document the per-row confidence as intentional or normalise the 95 rows to the table and let the grading code own the column.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01BP6MDZgidgzS79c75Ykhac
results.title: 95 published rows carry confidence values the grading table cannot produce

results.body:
Found in adversarial review of #528 (pre-existing; that PR neither caused nor worsened it).

17 records carry the same synonym text twice, compared casefolded:

```
Distilled_Water.yaml            'sterile dh2o'
Alk_So42.yaml                   'aluminum potassium sulfate'
Na2glycerophosphate5h2o.yaml    'na2glycerophosphate•5h2o(cas: 13408-09-8)'
Casein_Peptone.yaml             'casein hydrolysate', 'casein enzymic hydrolysate'
```

Count is identical on `origin/main`, so this predates the surface-form work. The
backfill's own duplicate check kept it from growing.

Low severity, but not nothing:

* `export_lists.py` emits one `label_index.csv` row per synonym, so a duplicate
  synonym produces two identical index rows for the same record. The lookup still
  resolves, but the index is larger than the corpus it describes and row counts stop
  being a usable measure of coverage — which is the number this work has been tracking
  throughout.
* The builder pipes synonyms into SSSOM `other`, where `_pipe` caps at
  `MAX_OTHER_ENTRIES = 50`. On a crowded row a duplicate consumes a slot that a distinct
  surface form would otherwise get, and the cap is documented as biting hardest on the
  hydrate families.

The fix is a de-duplicating pass over `synonyms`, casefolded, keeping the first
occurrence and preferring the more specific `synonym_type` when the duplicates disagree
(e.g. a `RAW_TEXT` and an `EXACT_SYNONYM` of the same string). Worth pairing with a guard
so it cannot recur, since several writers append synonyms and only some check first.
results.title: 17 records carry the same synonym twice, inflating the label index and the other cap

results.body:
Review finding on #732.

#732 retires 57 parent/sibling names from the salt, hydrate and tombstone records that wrongly carried them. For 46 of them the name still resolves — to the record that actually owns it. **11 now resolve to nothing:**

| surface form | was resolving to |
|---|---|
| `ferrous sulfate (anhydrous)` | was on `Feso4_X_7h2o` |
| `ferrous sulfate anhydrous` | was on `Feso4_X_7h2o` |
| `Manganese sulfate anhydrous` | was on `Mnso4_X_1_H2o` |
| `EDTA disodium (anhydrous)` | was on `Na2-edta_X_2_H2o` |
| `Edetate disodium anhydrous` | was on `Na2-edta_X_2_H2o` |
| `nickel(2+) sulfate` | was on `Niso4_X_6_H2o` |
| `nickel(2+) sulfate` | was on `Niso4_X_7_H2o` |
| `(2R)-2,3-dihydroxypropyl dihydrogen phosphate` | was on `Sn-Glycerol_3-phosphate_Lithium_Salt` |
| `sn-glycerol 3-(dihydrogen phosphate)` | was on `Sn-Glycerol_3-phosphate_Lithium_Salt` |
| `(2R)-2,3-dihydroxypropyl dihydrogen phosphate` | was on `Sn-glycerol_3-phosphate_Bis_Cyclohexylammonium_Salt` |
| `sn-glycerol 3-(dihydrogen phosphate)` | was on `Sn-glycerol_3-phosphate_Bis_Cyclohexylammonium_Salt` |

Each is a hydrate (or anhydrous) form that has **no record of its own**; its only home was a different hydrate's record, i.e. a wrong answer. Under Section 3 an unresolvable name is the correct state for a substance MIM does not hold — a recipe naming `FeSO4 x 5 H2O` should not silently become the heptahydrate — but it is still a gap, and the same shape as #656.

They belong to #459's hydrate cohort. Disposition per form: mint the hydrate (`cas:` or `kgmicrobe.compound:` + `broadMatch` to the anhydrous parent, Rule B1 registry row) if any recipe actually names it, or accept the gap if none does. I did not check occurrence counts here.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01ShSvr6po5J8sd7Ai4bRW9y

results.body:
## The check

For every record carrying both a `cas_rn` and a CHEBI `ontology_id`, ask which
CHEBI term ChEBI itself registers that CAS against:

```
CAS -> CHEBI index from chebi.db (oio:hasDbXref, 29,736 CAS numbers)

records with CAS + CHEBI id        1370
  CAS registered on THIS term      1074
  CAS not in ChEBI at all           206
  CAS registered on a DIFFERENT term  90   <- defect candidates
```

**This class is invisible to InChIKey comparison**, which is why it survived the
CAS-vs-structure checking done so far: the mis-mapped term is usually a
parent/grouping class with no structure at all, so there is no key to compare.
The failure mode is a name lookup landing on a parent while the CAS points at
the specific child.

## Cross-validation

The check independently rediscovers four defects found separately, one at a time,
by the research lane — before this query existed:

| record | CURIE | CAS points to |
|---|---|---|
| `Ca-pantothenate` | CHEBI:29032 `(R)-pantothenate` | **CHEBI:31345 Calcium pantothenate** (the #315 merge) |
| `02_Thiamine_Pyrophosphate` | CHEBI:9532 | CHEBI:18290 `…diphosphate chloride` |
| `Bicine` | CHEBI:39065 (structureless class) | CHEBI:40957 `N,N-bis(2-hydroxyethyl)glycine` |
| `Aluminium sulfate` | CHEBI:74772 (class) | CHEBI:74768 `aluminium sulfate (anhydrous)` |
| `Bisabolene` | CHEBI:49235 (family class) | CHEBI:49240 `alpha-bisabolene` |

Four separate agents reaching five of these independently, and a mechanical query
reproducing all of them, is good evidence the remaining 85 are real.

## Two sub-classes, different remedies — do not mass-apply

**(a) CURIE is a parent; the label names the specific child.** Fix the CURIE.
`Bicine` (a structureless grouping class with a disjunctive definition),
`Bisabolene` (family over 16 terms — note `C15H24` is shared by all of them, so
a formula check passes on the wrong term), `Ca-pantothenate`, `Aluminium sulfate`,
`alpha-Lactose` → `Alpha-lactose monohydrate`, `Carboxymethyl cellulose` →
`carboxymethylcellulose sodium`.

**(b) CURIE is correctly generic for a generic label; the *CAS* is over-specific.**
Fix or drop the CAS, not the mapping. `Arginine` (CHEBI:29016, stereo-agnostic —
correct for a bare label) whose CAS 74-79-3 is L-arginine's; `Ascorbic acid`
(CHEBI:22652) with L-ascorbic acid's CAS; `D-Ribose` with D-ribofuranose's.

Sub-class (b) is the same shape as the bare-anion convention in #319: a
deliberately generic term is right for a generic label, and it is the
*over-specific companion field* that is wrong. Getting this backwards would
break correct records.

## Suggested action

Triage the 90 into (a) and (b); the discriminator is whether the record's own
label is generic or specific. Then add the query as a standing check — it is
cheap, needs only `chebi.db`, and catches a class nothing else does.

Also worth noting the 206 "CAS not in ChEBI at all": not a defect by itself, but
it is the population where a wrong CAS can hide indefinitely, since neither this
check nor an InChIKey comparison can adjudicate it.

## Provenance

Proposed by the Claude research lane after it hit the same shape three times
(`Bicine`, `Bisabolene`, `02_Thiamine_Pyrophosphate`) and observed that InChIKey
comparison structurally cannot catch it. Verified repo-wide against chebi.db.
Related: #315, #316, #317, #319.
results.title: 90 records whose CAS-RN is registered in ChEBI against a different term than their CURIE

results.body:
Found by cross-checking MIM against **CultureBotAI/CultureMech#272**, which independently regrounds the same labels — and is right where MIM is wrong.

This is the identity half of #321, still open for these seven. Each names a hydrate, sits on an anhydrous or generic ChEBI term, and ChEBI **has** the specific hydrate term, so `MAPPING_SEMANTICS` §3 **step 1** applies and nothing needs minting:

| record | currently on | should be |
|---|---|---|
| `Chromium(III) Chloride Hexahydrate` | `CHEBI:53351` chromium(3+) trichloride | `CHEBI:53442` …hexahydrate |
| `CoSO4 x 7 H2O` | `CHEBI:53470` cobalt(2+) sulfate | `CHEBI:91244` …heptahydrate |
| `FeSO4 x 7H2O` | `CHEBI:75832` iron(2+) sulfate **(anhydrous)** | `CHEBI:75836` …heptahydrate |
| `MgSO4·7H2O` | `CHEBI:32599` magnesium sulfate | `CHEBI:31795` …heptahydrate |
| `MnSO4 x 1 H2O` | `CHEBI:86360` manganese(II) sulfate | `CHEBI:86364` …monohydrate |
| `Na2SeO3·5H2O` | `CHEBI:48843` disodium selenite | `CHEBI:131361` …pentahydrate |
| `NiSO4 x 7 H2O` | `CHEBI:53001` nickel sulfate | `CHEBI:53504` …heptahydrate |

`FeSO4 x 7H2O` is the sharpest: its term is explicitly labelled **"(anhydrous)"** while the record's own label says 7 H2O.

## Two complications, both worth settling in the same pass

**1. Some targets are already held.** `CHEBI:75836` is held by `FeSO4 x 7 H2O` (note the space — a near-duplicate of `FeSO4 x 7H2O`, and one of the ten pairs recorded on #334). So this is a promotion for some and a **merge** for others; `fix_hydrate_collapse.py` already handles both shapes and distinguishes them by whether the target identifier is taken.

**2. #342 decided hydrate→anhydrous is `closeMatch`.** That decision was about records whose hydrate has *no* ChEBI term. These seven do have one, so they move to `EXACT_MATCH` on the specific term and leave the closeMatch question behind entirely — worth stating explicitly so the two decisions are not read as conflicting.

## Provenance

Surfaced by diffing CultureMech#272's chosen `term.id` against MIM's answer for every name it changes: 27 changed, 11 agree with MIM, **16 disagree**. On the hydrate subset the disagreement is MIM's fault, and these 7 are it. (The remaining disagreements are covered by CultureBotAI/CultureMech#260 and by one genuine defect in #272 flagged there.)
results.title: 7 hydrate records sit on the anhydrous term while ChEBI has the specific hydrate

results.body:
## The check

Flag any record whose `preferred_term` names a hydrate (`x n H2O`, `·nH2O`,
`hydrate`) while its recorded formula/SMILES/InChI contain **no water
component**. Purely mechanical.

**Result: 26 records.**

## Why the existing CAS-vs-structure check cannot see this

Both compared fields are populated from the same ChEBI term by
`AUTO_BACKFILL_CHEBI_CHEMISTRY`, so they agree **by construction**. The check
compares the record against itself; the *label* is the only field carrying the
contradicting information, and nothing was comparing against it.

## The sharper pattern: one term absorbing many distinct hydrates

**10 ontology terms carry 26 distinct hydrate labels between them:**

| term | absorbs |
|---|---|
| CHEBI:34683 | `Na2HPO4 x 2/3/6/7/12 H2O` — **five** different hydrates |
| CHEBI:35696 | `CoCl2 x 2/4/6 H2O` |
| CHEBI:34887 | `NiCl2 x 2/5/6 H2O` |
| CHEBI:75832 | `FeSO4 x 5/6/7 H2O` |
| CHEBI:23414 | `CuSO4 x 2/4 H2O` |
| CHEBI:30812 | `FeCl2 x 6/7 H2O` |
| CHEBI:86360 | `MnSO4 x 1/7 H2O` |
| CHEBI:53001 | `NiSO4 x 6/7 H2O` |

Different hydrates are different substances with different formula weights and
different CAS numbers. Collapsed onto one term they are indistinguishable
downstream — a recipe calling for the heptahydrate and one calling for the
dihydrate become the same node.

**The assignment is demonstrably arbitrary.** Magnesium sulfate splits across two
terms *by notation rather than by chemistry*:

```
CHEBI:32599  <- "MgSO4 x 6 H2O",  "MgSO4·7H2O"
CHEBI:31795  <- "MgSO4 x 7 H2O",  "MgSO4·H2O"
```

The **same** hydration number (7) lands on two different terms depending on
whether the label was written `x 7 H2O` or `·7H2O`. That is lexical matching
with no chemistry behind it.

One record states the contradiction outright: `Na2-EDTA x 2 H2O` carries
`ontology_label: EDTA disodium salt (anhydrous)`.

## Triage forks three ways — do not mass-apply

Established from three worked cases:

1. **The label is wrong.** `CaSO4 x 7 H2O` — no calcium sulfate heptahydrate
   exists (ChEBI has anhydrous/hemi/dihydrate only). Probably a `2`→`7` slip,
   but confirming needs the source recipes read. MediaDive maps
   `CaSO4 x 2 H2O` correctly, so it does distinguish these when they are real.
2. **The label is right and the ontology is deficient.** `CeCl3 x 7 H2O` is the
   standard commercial form; ChEBI has **no** cerium chloride hydrate at all.
   Ignoring the waters here is a **51% formula-weight error** (246 → 373).
   Candidate for a registry term.
3. **Neither side is definite.** `Cefsulodin sodium salt hydrate` — no hydrate
   term in any ontology *and* the label states no hydration number. Nothing to
   encode; the fix is dropping `EXACT_MATCH` and recording why.

So a lexical `x n H2O` sweep would fix (1) and corrupt (2).

## Suggested action

Add the detector as a standing check, then triage the 26 by the fork above.
The `Na2HPO4` five-way and `CoCl2`/`NiCl2` three-way collapses are the highest
value — they are the cases where distinct media ingredients have become
indistinguishable.

## Provenance

Detector proposed by the Claude research lane after the CAS-vs-structure check
passed on three defective records in one batch, with the correct diagnosis of
why it structurally could not catch them. Verified repo-wide.
Related: #315, #317, #320.
results.title: 26 hydrate-named records map to anhydrous terms; 10 terms absorb multiple distinct hydrates
